lessons.title: When and how much to water
lessons.html:
When and how much to water

All plants need water to live. In South Africa many areas are dry, and towns often have water limits. So we must water well, but never waste water.

When to water

  • Water early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Less water is lost to the sun and wind.
  • Do not water in the heat of the day. Much of the water dries up before the plant can use it.
  • Check the soil before you water. Push your finger into the soil. If it is damp below the top, wait. If it is dry, water.
  • Follow the town's water rules. Some days or times may not be allowed.

Signs a plant needs water

  • Leaves hang down (wilt) in the morning.
  • Lawn turns grey-blue and footprints stay in it.
  • Soil is dry and hard.

How much water

Water deeply and not too often. A deep watering makes roots grow down, where the soil stays damp longer. A little water every day keeps roots at the top, and the plants suffer on hot days.

Different plants need different amounts:

PlantsWater needs
New plants and seedlingsOften, until roots grow
LawnsMedium to high
Flower beds with annualsMedium to high
Established trees and shrubsDeep watering less often
Succulents and aloesVery little

Too much water

Too much water is also bad. Roots rot, leaves turn yellow, and water runs away into the street. If water runs off the soil, stop and let it soak in first.

lessons.title: Watering with hoses, cans and sprinklers
lessons.html:
Watering with hoses, cans and sprinklers

Watering can

Use a can with a rose (the sprinkler head) for seedlings and small plants. The rose gives soft drops that do not wash soil away.

Hose

  • Use a spray nozzle on the hose. Choose a soft spray, not a hard jet.
  • Water the soil at the base of the plant, not the leaves. Wet leaves can get fungus.
  • Move slowly. Give each plant enough water to soak in deeply.
  • Do not pull the hose over flower beds. It breaks plants.
  • Roll up the hose after use. Do not leave it on paths where people can trip.

Sprinklers and irrigation systems

  • Check that the sprinkler water lands on the lawn or bed, not on walls, paving or the street.
  • Look for broken sprinkler heads, leaking pipes and blocked drippers. Report them to your team leader.
  • Run the sprinkler only for the time your team leader says.
  • Do not run sprinklers in strong wind.

Saving water

  • Put mulch on beds to keep the soil damp.
  • Group plants with the same water needs together.
  • Close taps fully. Fix or report leaks at once. A dripping tap wastes many litres a day.
  • Use rainwater from tanks if the client has them.

Safety

Keep electrical cables and plugs away from water. Do not drink water from irrigation or borehole lines unless you know it is safe. Wet paving is slippery; walk carefully.

Key points

  • Water early morning or late afternoon.
  • Check the soil with your finger before watering.
  • Water deeply and less often; water the soil, not the leaves.
  • Report leaks and broken sprinklers.
  • Use mulch and follow water rules to save water.
